candidate_verticals.label: Manufacturing establishments
candidate_verticals.research_hypothesis: Manufacturers with recurring for-hire LTL invoices may have date-sensitive accessorial, freight class, discount and contract complexity; demand and error frequency are unproven.
candidate_verticals.next_falsification: Identify a rights-cleared sample of actual paid for-hire LTL invoices and dated rate documents from consenting establishments, including invoices with no errors.
candidate_verticals.prohibited_inference: Manufacturing commodity-shipment value cannot become LTL billings, annual recovery rate or buyer willingness.

candidate_verticals.label: Wholesale establishments
candidate_verticals.research_hypothesis: Wholesalers with multiple carrier contracts may be worth testing for invoice reconciliation complexity, but no observed invoice mix, actual paid charges or recovery incidence has been supplied.
candidate_verticals.next_falsification: Before ranking buyers, document real LTL versus parcel and company-owned transport share, contract access, incumbent audit tools and buyer authority in a permissioned study.
candidate_verticals.prohibited_inference: The source's $8.1T value of shipped goods is not freight charges, fees, audit market TAM or revenue.

candidate_verticals.label: Warehousing and distribution auxiliaries
candidate_verticals.research_hypothesis: Distribution establishments appear in the CFS sampling universe, but this press release does not publish an isolated warehouse truck/freight-invoice volume metric.
candidate_verticals.next_falsification: Extract 2022 official GAS18 (NAICS × mode × distance) with source dictionary, then separately verify which movements produce third-party LTL invoices.
candidate_verticals.prohibited_inference: Survey coverage alone cannot establish distribution-center market size or invoice-error risk.

Understand mode mix by establishment category and shipment weight; not freight invoice charges or paid carrier spend.
